title: Proton pump inhibitors are not associated with an increased risk of Clostridioides difficile infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
authors: Floria DE, Obeidat M, Váncsa S, Kávási SB, Földvári-Nagy L, Hegyi P, et al.
population: Randomised trials in adults comparing PPIs with placebo or other therapies, searched 15 April 2025; of the 8 trials against placebo (14,946 PPI, 14,934 placebo), six enrolled hospitalised patients given short courses for stress-ulcer or acute coronary syndrome bleeding prophylaxis and two enrolled outpatients on long-term antithrombotic bleeding prophylaxis, among them COMPASS (median 3 years)
authorConflicts: No potential conflicts of interest were disclosed.
result: C. difficile infection, PPI against non-PPI: RR 1.19 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.89; 8 trials, 29,880 participants); against H2-receptor blockers RR 0.72 (0.49 to 1.07; 4 trials, 27,254 participants); against potassium-competitive acid blockers RR 1.23 (0.43 to 3.55; 3 trials, 1645 participants). Qualitative synthesis: other enteric infections and small intestinal bacterial overgrowth may be more common with PPIs; in COMPASS, enteric infections 119 of 8791 (1.4%) against 90 of 8807 (1.0%); in a trial in severe acute pancreatitis, duodenal aerobic bacterial overgrowth after 7 days in 29 of 33 given esomeprazole against 15 of 33 without (RR 1.93, 1.30 to 2.86).
